subject: using Stan's generated quantities block to perform computations on already-computed posterior simulations?

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: using Stan's generated quantities block to perform computations on already-computed posterior simulations?
parts:
Hi, I’m stuck on something. In some ways it’s no big deal cos I could do it in R, but I’d like to stay within Stan if possible.

It’s a question about generated quantities, and it comes from the project with Sebastian and Amy on the incorporation of aggregate data into a Bayesian analysis.

Currently I have a Stan program (attached in this message) that I wrote. The program works as follows:

- In the model block, I compute the log posterior given the data matrix y.

- In the generated quantities block, I first simulate an external parameter delta (from a prior distribution input into the Stan model) and then I simulate a fake data matrix y_tilde. For each posterior simulation draw (i.e., in each call to the generated quantities block), I simulate 100 fake data matrices and then compute their covariance matrix, then from there I compute an importance weight which is used in later calculations.

What I’ve been doing is iterating: I start with a guess of the prior for the external parameter delta, then I run the Stan program, then I use the results to come up with a new prior, then I re-run the Stan program, etc.

But, what I realized is, I shouldn’t really need to be re-fitting the model each time. Really all I should need to do is to re-run the generated quantities block with the updated prior but with the same posterior simulations of the parameters from the model block.

So, here’s my question: Can we call Stan using existing posterior simulations? I think the answer is No, so that I’ll just have to do my generating in R. Which I can do, it just seems too bad that I can’t do it all in Stan.

Any help would be appreciated. It’s not urgent but it’s buggin me. Thanks.

A

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] using Stan's generated quantities block to perform computations on already-computed posterior simulations?
parts:
I think the best way to do this is to user-define a Stan function that ends in _rng

matrix foo_rng(matrix input) {
  // do random-number generation
  // return whatever
}

export that function to R (only rstan 2.6.3 is capable of doing this at the moment), and then call that function from R.

E.g. I did this to calculate the WAIC from R

# WAIC implied by normal log-likelihood
vector WAIC(vector y, matrix X, /* N rows */
            vector intercept, matrix beta,
           /* parameters all have S draws */
           vector sigma) {

  vector[2] out; out <- rep_vector(0,2);
  for(i in 1:rows(X)) {
    vector[rows(beta)] ll;
    vector[rows(beta)] mu; mu <- intercept +
     beta * transpose(row(X,i));
    for(j in 1:rows(beta)) ll[j] <-
      normal_log(y[i], mu[j], sigma[j]);
    out[1] <- out[1] + log(mean(exp(ll)));
    out[2] <- out[2] + variance(ll);
  }
  out[1] <- -2 * (out[1] - out[2]);
  return out; # out[1] is WAIC, out[2] is p_WAIC
}

Ben
On Friday, March 27, 2015 at 5:51:11 PM UTC-4, Andrew Gelman wrote:

Hi—I thought of that but this is not so natural.  For example, suppose the parameter “a” in the model is a vector of length 2, and we run Stan and get 2000 simulations.  Then we’d have to declare “a” as a 2000 x 2 matrix.  But that is contrary to the spirit of probabilistic programming.

Hi Ben!

Just to clarify: The wait function you show is part of the Stan model which you then call in R via the magic Rcpp trick which you formerly called "testify", right?

Awesome that this is already in Stan 2.6.3 which triggers, of course, immediately the question when this will be available as rstan or even better available on cran?

As I recall, the wrapped Stan functions always needed recompilation due to Rcpp - has there been a workaround for this, i.e. is a make-like behavior possible by now or should we direct this to the Rcpp maintainers? If Rcpp is the right address, what feature of Rcpp are you specifically using which one cannot cache like usual Stan model objects?

Best,
Sebastian

On Saturday, March 28, 2015 at 7:11:12 AM UTC-4, Sebastian Weber wrote:
Just to clarify: The wait function you show is part of the Stan model which you then call in R via the magic Rcpp trick which you formerly called "testify", right?
That is correct. I think the function will get renamed expose_stan_functions() or something.
Awesome that this is already in Stan 2.6.3 which triggers, of course, immediately the question when this will be available as rstan or even better available on cran?

That is really the same question as we are just waiting for StanHeaders 2.6.3 to be approved by CRAN before we can upload rstan 2.6.3 because rstan doesn't build with the StanHeaders 2.6.0-10 that is currently on CRAN.

As I recall, the wrapped Stan functions always needed recompilation due to Rcpp - has there been a workaround for this, i.e. is a make-like behavior possible by now or should we direct this to the Rcpp maintainers? If Rcpp is the right address, what feature of Rcpp are you specifically using which one cannot cache like usual Stan model objects?

As far as I know, it is not currently possible with Rcpp but it doesn't really have anything to do with Stan. If you just run Rcpp's example of sourceCpp, it does not work when reloaded in a new R session on the same computer

library(Rcpp)
sourceCpp(code='
  #include <Rcpp.h>

  // [[Rcpp::export]]
  int fibonacci(const int x) {
    if (x == 0) return(0);
    if (x == 1) return(1);
    return (fibonacci(x - 1)) + fibonacci(x - 2);
  }'
)
fibonacci(5) # 5
saveRDS(fibonacci, file = "fibonacci.rda")
q()

and then restart R

library(Rcpp)
fibonacci <- readRDS("fibonacci.rda")
fibonacci(5) # error

Ben
